assignment:
Some of your friends perform community service. For example, some tutor elementary school children and others clean up litter. They think helping the community is very important. But other friends of yours think community service takes too much time away from what they need or want to do. 
Your principal is deciding whether to require all students to perform community service. 
Write a letter to your principal in which you take a position on whether students should be required to perform community service. Support your position with examples.
essay_1:
Dear Principal,

I think our school should make every student do some community service, as long as the number of hours stays reasonable.

Some of my friends tutor second graders at Lincoln Elementary after school. At first they only went because a teacher asked them to, but now they talk about "their kids" all the time and say it is fun. One of them even wants to be a teacher. She never would have figured that out if nobody pushed her to try it.

Other friends spent a Saturday picking up trash along the creek behind the park. They filled twenty bags. The next week people were walking their dogs there again. A few hours of work changed the place for the whole neighborhood.

I know some kids think service will take time away from homework, sports, or jobs. That makes sense, but ten or fifteen hours a year with lots of choices of when and where is not a big deal for anyone.

Service teaches responsibility and helps our town, but it only works if the school makes it count. If we don't require it, most kids won't sign up. If we do, I think a lot of them will end up glad they went.

Sincerely,
A concerned student
essay_2:
Dear Principal,

I think our school should make every student do community service, but only if it isnt to many hours.

Some of my friends tutor second graders at Lincoln Elementary after school. At first they only went because a teacher told them to. Now they talk about "their kids" all the time and one of them even wants to be a teacher when she grows up. She never would of found that out if nobody made her try it.

Some other friends spent a Saturday picking up trash by the creek behind the park. They filled like twenty bags! The next week people were walking there dogs there again. Just a couple hours of work made it better for the whole neighborhood.

I know some kids are worried that service will take time away from homework or sports or jobs. That makes sense. But if it was only ten or fifteen hours a year and you could pick when and where you do it, nobody would get overloaded.

Community service teaches kids to be responsible and it also helps our town. So please make it part of our school.

Sincerely,
A concerned student
